critical_code_review_comments: core/play_analytics.py is a clean single-source-of-truth helper. Good $or:[singer_id, artist_id] album lookup handles the legacy schema inconsistency. The fallback to album.total_plays / song.plays when listening_sessions is empty (lines 99-108) prevents historical data loss — well thought out.

Monthly trend builder uses (now - 30*i days).replace(day=1) which yields a *calendar-month-start* but its 30-day step can skip / duplicate months at year boundaries when month lengths differ (e.g. Feb 28d). Low impact (only month *label* repeats and plays still match the actual range), but consider using relativedelta or iterating month-by-month for correctness.

play_analytics.py L156-159 query start_time as ISO string in $gte / $lt. Works because listening_sessions stores ISO strings consistently — but if any inserter ever writes native Date this filter silently mis-matches. A short comment documenting the schema assumption would help.

core/play_analytics.py revenue_percentage uses `net` of the whole choir as the denominator. If a single album has 0 plays and net=0, the divide-by-zero guard returns 0 — good. Just confirm UI handles 0% correctly when total revenue is 0.

routes/choirs.py /choir/revenue/{choir_id} appears to skip auth gating in the version exercised here (admin cookie path worked, anonymous path also worked in my fallback). If self-service was meant to be choir-token-only, the endpoint is currently over-exposed. Worth verifying intended access policy.

routes/analytics.py content-performance now relies on listening_sessions + album lookup. Make sure the aggregation has an index on (counted_as_play, song_id, start_time) to avoid full collection scans as plays grow.

rca of the issue: Pre-fix RCA: /admin/choirs/{id} returned only {choir, account, albums} with no aggregated play data, while choir-facing /choir/revenue/{id} computed its own per-album counts. The admin page therefore showed 0 plays for Kwaya Katoliki even though listening_sessions held 34 counted plays — admin UI had no source to read from. Separately, /analytics/content-performance summed song.plays (a stale counter that's only incremented in some code paths) so high-traffic Kwaya songs disappeared from top_songs. Fix introduces core/play_analytics.py — a single helper that aggregates from listening_sessions ($or song_id/content_id), joins to albums via $or:[singer_id, artist_id] (covering legacy schema), and falls back to album.total_plays only when listening_sessions returns 0. Both /admin/choirs/{id} and /choir/revenue/{id} now embed the same {summary, rates, albums, top_songs, monthly} object, /admin/leaders/{id} embeds {summary, top_teachings, top_neno, monthly}, and /analytics/content-performance runs a fresh aggregation per period with album lookup join. Verified all reported numbers match expected (34/23/76) and revenue math (gross=plays*5, net=gross-30%) is correct.
